graphEvents.label: Which mechanism brings plain chat onto the command workflow
Hub mode registries already bind modes to commands
Recommended mechanism is brief command plus AGENTS.md Gate 2 rule

label: The hook is advisory and fails open; it never replaces explicit skill loading and never blocks the prompt on an advisor failure, so it cannot redirect a chat request into a command by itself.

The brief names recommended skills; only doctor commands appear as runnable /doctor: strings, so non-doctor commands have no model-visible invocation in the one prompt-time channel reaching all runtimes.
Gate 2 tells the model to use the brief or advisor CLI and emit SKILL ROUTING, never to run a command workflow, so a chat-only request is steered toward a skill even when a command owns the workflow.
PLAN-WORKFLOW LOCK forbids hand-rolling a plan-named workflow but says nothing about discovering that an unnamed command owns the request, so the prohibition cannot fire when the user types prose.
The brief is silent exactly when a chat-only user needs it: the measured planning and research prompts return zero recommendations at the shipped 0.8 threshold.

A runner refusal exists only as normative prose: deep-research says it is invoked exclusively through /deep:research:auto or :confirm, but that SKILL.md loads after the skill is chosen, which is after the hand-roll decision.

Hub mode registries already bind modes to commands: sk-doc records a command for every mode and states command-bridge modes are reached only via their command, while system-deep-loop records /deep:research with lexical routing.

Recommended mechanism: the brief carries command, policy and ownerSkillId from the hub registry, and Gate 2 gains one rule to load and execute the command document when policy is run or offer it and wait when policy is ask.

Where the brief does not arrive, the mechanism needs a backstop: Gate 2 should also say that with no brief the model asks the advisor CLI before hand-rolling, because delivery can fail open to the directives fallback.

reason: The hook is advisory, fails open and cannot dispatch a command
The refusal prose loads after the skill is chosen, too late to prevent the hand-roll

direction: A static command list in AGENTS.md
reason: 45 commands with modes and arguments would drift and consume the rule budget
